r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative:
Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a
verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated
code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list,
shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality,
comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment
calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards -- an override
needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to
.agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (from
templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py
.agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an
unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's
postcondition command resolves the record path from <work-id> alone -- the
same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey -- so no
separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only
if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it
through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is
`retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There,
--authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never
a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently
skip this item.

postconditions.statement: verify_fowler_pass.py exits 0 on the Fowler-pass record -- refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override

constraints: Fowler smells are subordinate to documented repo standards; never hard violations
an override (smell not flagged because a standard wins) needs a logged reason

claim.text: The Fowler-pass verdict spans the ENTIRE diff, not one narrow question the way the survey's other six items do -- a false 'absent' or an unlogged override lets a real code smell through with no other checkpoint behind it. It is the one item in either role spec whose scope is genuinely broad rather than narrowly targeted, which is why the escalation belongs here and not on a throwaway stand-in.
claim.enforcement: NOT machine-enforced here -- no postcondition is injected for a large claim on a `survey` spec. `checklist_engine.record()` on a survey item evaluates only command-kind postconditions (survey-record-check-scope, #422) and leaves an artifact-kind postcondition like the one `gated` specs inject permanently unevaluated; `checklist_engine.consolidate()` reads only each item's stored `result` field and nothing else (#328). An injected postcondition here would be silently inert, not a real gate -- so none is injected. The tier this gate hands back to (see `directives.handback.hand_back_to`) must adjudicate this claim itself.
